items.name: AnyError
items.doc: The application-level error box. Any `E: Error` converts into it with `?`.

items.name: chain
items.doc: The messages of this error and the errors it wraps, outermost first.

items.name: downcast
items.doc: The boxed error as `E` (taken from the expected type), or `None`.

items.name: BigInt
items.doc: An arbitrary-precision integer.

items.name: from
items.doc: The exact value of an `Int`.

items.name: parse
items.doc: The integer written in the text.

items.name: pow
items.doc: `self` raised to the power `exponent` (Kalam has no `**`), exactly. `x.pow(0)` is 1. Panics on a negative exponent, and when the result would have 65536 bits or more.

items.name: to_int
items.doc: The value as an `Int`, or `None` outside the 64-bit range.

items.name: Bool
items.doc: `true` or `false`. Conditions must be `Bool`: there is no truthiness.

items.name: Bytes
items.doc: An immutable byte array.

items.name: len
items.doc: The number of bytes.

items.name: slice
items.signature: fn slice(self, from: Int, to: Int) -> Bytes
items.doc: The bytes from index `from` up to, not including, `to`.

items.name: to_base64
items.doc: Standard base64 text.

items.name: to_hex
items.doc: Lowercase hexadecimal text.

items.name: Cell
items.doc: The only shared mutable state. `update` is atomic because its function cannot suspend.

items.name: get
items.doc: The current value.

items.name: new
items.doc: A new cell holding `value`.

items.name: set
items.doc: Replaces the value.

items.name: update
items.doc: Replaces the value with `f(value)`, atomically.

items.name: Clock
items.doc: The current time and timers.

items.name: now
items.doc: The current instant.

items.name: today
items.doc: Today's date in `zone`.

items.name: Command
items.doc: A program and its argv built by `cmd"…"`. There is no raw form.

items.name: add_days
items.doc: The date `days` later (earlier when negative).

items.name: day
items.doc: The day of the month, 1-31.

items.name: format_hijri
items.doc: The Hijri (Umm al-Qura) date as text.

items.name: month
items.doc: The Gregorian month, 1-12.

items.name: new
items.signature: fn new(year: Int, month: Int, day: Int) -> Result[Date, TimeError]
items.doc: The date with this year, month (1-12) and day, or an error.

items.name: to_iso
items.doc: ISO 8601 text, such as `2027-01-31`.

items.name: year
items.doc: The Gregorian year.

items.name: all
items.signature: fn all[T: Row](self, query: Sql) -> Result[List[T], DbError]
items.doc: Every row of `query`, decoded by column name into `T` (from the expected type).

items.name: exec
items.signature: fn exec(self, query: Sql) -> Result[Int, DbError]
items.doc: Runs `query` and returns the number of rows affected.

items.name: one
items.signature: fn one[T: Row](self, query: Sql) -> Result[Option[T], DbError]
items.doc: The first row of `query`, or `None`.

items.name: transaction
items.signature: fn transaction[T, E: From[DbError]](self, body: fn(Db) -> Result[T, E]) -> Result[T, E]
items.doc: Runs `body` in a transaction: it commits on `Ok` and rolls back on `Err`, on panic and on cancellation.

items.name: Decimal
items.doc: An exact base-10 number with 34 significant digits. There is no `/`: use `div`.

items.name: div
items.signature: fn div(self, other: Decimal, scale: Int, rounding: Rounding) -> Decimal
items.doc: `self / other` rounded to `scale` fraction digits. Panics when `other` is zero.

items.name: from
items.doc: The exact value of an `Int`.

items.name: parse
items.doc: The exact `Decimal` written in the text.

items.name: pow
items.doc: `self` raised to the power `exponent` (Kalam has no `**`), exactly: `x.pow(3)` is `x * x * x`. `x.pow(0)` is 1. Panics on a negative exponent, and when the result needs more than 34 digits or its exponent is out of range.

items.name: round
items.signature: fn round(self, scale: Int, rounding: Rounding = .HalfEven) -> Decimal
items.doc: The value rounded to `scale` fraction digits.

items.name: Decode
items.doc: Schema-first input (spec §18.3). Explicit `@derive(Decode)`.

items.name: days
items.doc: `count` days of 24 hours.

items.name: hours
items.doc: `count` hours.

items.name: minutes
items.doc: `count` minutes.

items.name: ms
items.doc: `count` milliseconds.

items.name: plus
items.doc: The sum of the two durations.

items.name: seconds
items.doc: `count` seconds.

items.name: to_ms
items.doc: The whole milliseconds, truncated toward zero.

items.name: Encode
items.doc: JSON and wire output. Explicit `@derive(Encode)`; never for `Secret[T]` (K0612).

items.name: Env
items.doc: Environment variables.

items.name: get
items.doc: The variable's value, or `None` when it is unset. A literal key that looks secret (`*_KEY`, `*_SECRET`, `*_TOKEN`, `PASSWORD`) is K1503: use `secret`.

items.name: only
items.doc: An `Env` that can read only `keys`.

items.name: secret
items.doc: The variable's value as a `Secret`, or `None` when it is unset.

items.name: Eq
items.doc: `==` and `!=`. Derived automatically when every component is `Eq`.

items.name: Err
items.doc: The failure case of `Result`.

items.name: Error
items.doc: An error value: `.message()` is used by `AnyError`, `main` and logs.

items.name: Float
items.doc: An IEEE-754 binary64 number. Not `Eq`, `Ord` or `Hash`: use `total_cmp`, `near` and `is_nan` (DR-23).

items.name: abs
items.doc: The absolute value.

items.name: is_nan
items.doc: True for NaN.

items.name: near
items.signature: fn near(self, other: Float, tol: Float) -> Bool
items.doc: True when `self` and `other` differ by at most `tol`.

items.name: pow
items.doc: `self` raised to the power `exponent` (Kalam has no `**`), with IEEE semantics, as `math.pow`: `(2.0).pow(0.5)` is the square root of 2.

items.name: to_int
items.doc: The integer value, or `None` for NaN, infinities and values outside the `Int` range. The fraction is truncated toward zero.

items.name: total_cmp
items.doc: IEEE total order: the only total comparison on `Float`.

items.name: From
items.doc: The conversion `?` uses when the error types differ (spec §14.3 rule 2).

items.name: Fs
items.doc: Files.

items.name: dir
items.signature: fn dir(self, root: Path) -> Result[Fs, FsError]
items.doc: An `Fs` rooted at `root`: `..` and symlinks that leave the root are refused.

items.name: exists
items.doc: True when the path exists.

items.name: list
items.signature: fn list(self, dir: Path) -> Result[List[String], FsError]
items.doc: The names in a directory, sorted.

items.name: read_bytes
items.signature: fn read_bytes(self, file: Path) -> Result[Bytes, FsError]
items.doc: The whole file as bytes.

items.name: read_only
items.doc: An `Fs` that cannot write.

items.name: read_text
items.signature: fn read_text(self, file: Path) -> Result[String, FsError]
items.doc: The whole file as UTF-8 text.

items.name: write_text
items.signature: fn write_text(self, file: Path, text: String) -> Result[(), FsError]
items.doc: Creates or replaces the file with `text`.

items.name: Hash
items.doc: `Map` and `Set` keys. Derived automatically when every component is `Hash`.

items.name: Html
items.doc: HTML built by `html"…"` with contextual auto-escaping.

items.name: join
items.doc: The fragments one after another.

items.name: render
items.doc: The HTML text.

items.name: from
items.doc: Any other error is a 500; the details are logged, not shown.

items.name: from
items.doc: A database error is a 500; the details are logged, not shown.

items.name: from
items.doc: A decoding error is a 400.

items.name: date
items.doc: The date of this instant in `zone`.

items.name: plus
items.doc: The instant `amount` later (earlier for a negative duration).

items.name: since
items.doc: The duration from `earlier` to `self`.

items.name: to_iso
items.doc: ISO 8601 text in UTC, such as `2027-01-31T09:30:00Z`.

items.name: to_unix_ms
items.doc: Milliseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z.

items.name: Int
items.doc: A 64-bit signed integer in [-2^63, 2^63 - 1] on every backend (D18). `+ - *` trap on overflow, `//` floors, `%` takes the sign of the divisor, and `/` returns `Float`.

items.name: abs
items.doc: The absolute value. Panics on the minimum `Int`.

items.name: bit_and
items.doc: Bitwise AND of the 64-bit two's complement forms (Kalam has no `&`).

items.name: bit_or
items.doc: Bitwise OR of the 64-bit two's complement forms (Kalam has no `|`).

items.name: bit_xor
items.doc: Bitwise exclusive OR of the 64-bit two's complement forms (Kalam has no `^`).

items.name: checked_add
items.doc: `self + other`, or `None` on overflow.

items.name: checked_mul
items.doc: `self * other`, or `None` on overflow.

items.name: checked_sub
items.doc: `self - other`, or `None` on overflow.

items.name: pow
items.doc: `self` raised to the power `exponent` (Kalam has no `**`). Panics on overflow and on a negative exponent. `0.pow(0)` is 1.

items.name: saturating_add
items.doc: `self + other`, clamped to the 64-bit bounds.

items.name: shift_left
items.doc: The 64-bit two's complement form shifted left by `by` bits; bits shifted out are dropped. Panics when `by` is outside `0..=63`.

items.name: shift_right
items.doc: Arithmetic shift right by `by` bits: the sign is kept, so the result is `self` divided by 2 to the power `by`, rounded down. Panics when `by` is outside `0..=63`.

items.name: to_float
items.doc: The same value as a `Float` (exact up to 2^53).

items.name: to_string
items.doc: The decimal text with ASCII digits, a stable wire format (§6.2).

items.name: wrapping_add
items.doc: `self + other`, wrapping around at the 64-bit bounds.

items.name: Iterable
items.doc: What `for` iterates: `List`, `Set`, `Map` (as pairs), ranges.

items.name: List
items.doc: An ordered, immutable list. `xs[i]` panics when out of bounds; `xs.get(i)` does not.

items.name: all
items.signature: fn all(self, predicate: fn(T) -> Bool) -> Bool
items.doc: True when `predicate` is true for every element (and for the empty list).

items.name: any
items.signature: fn any(self, predicate: fn(T) -> Bool) -> Bool
items.doc: True when `predicate` is true for at least one element.

items.name: append
items.doc: A copy with `item` added at the end.

items.name: contains
items.doc: True when some element equals `item`.

items.name: enumerate
items.doc: Each element with its index: `(0, x0), (1, x1), …`.

items.name: filter
items.signature: fn filter(self, keep: fn(T) -> Bool) -> List[T]
items.doc: The elements for which `keep` is true.

items.name: find
items.signature: fn find(self, predicate: fn(T) -> Bool) -> Option[T]
items.doc: The first element for which `predicate` is true.

items.name: first
items.doc: The first element, or `None` for the empty list.

items.name: fold
items.signature: fn fold[A](self, init: A, f: fn(A, T) -> A) -> A
items.doc: `f(…f(f(init, x0), x1)…)` over the elements in order.

items.name: get
items.doc: The element at `index`, or `None` when it is out of bounds.

items.name: group_by
items.signature: fn group_by[K: Eq + Hash](self, key: fn(T) -> K) -> Map[K, List[T]]
items.doc: The elements grouped by `key`, groups in order of first appearance.

items.name: insert
items.signature: fn insert(self, index: Int, item: T) -> List[T]
items.doc: A copy with `item` inserted before `index`. Panics when `index > len`.

items.name: is_empty
items.doc: True when the list has no elements.

items.name: last
items.doc: The last element, or `None` for the empty list.

items.name: len
items.doc: The number of elements.

items.name: map
items.signature: fn map[U](self, f: fn(T) -> U) -> List[U]
items.doc: `f` applied to every element, in order.

items.name: remove
items.doc: A copy without the element at `index`. Panics when out of bounds.

items.name: set
items.signature: fn set(self, index: Int, value: T) -> List[T]
items.doc: A copy with the element at `index` replaced. Panics when out of bounds.

items.name: skip
items.doc: The elements after the first `count`.

items.name: sort_by
items.signature: fn sort_by(self, cmp: @sync fn(T, T) -> Ordering) -> List[T]
items.doc: A stable sort by a comparator that cannot suspend.

items.name: sorted
items.doc: A stable sort in ascending `Ord` order.

items.name: sum
items.doc: The sum of the elements. Panics on overflow.

items.name: take
items.doc: The first `count` elements (all of them when there are fewer).

items.name: zip
items.signature: fn zip[U](self, other: List[U]) -> List[(T, U)]
items.doc: Pairs of elements at the same index; the longer list is cut to the shorter one.

items.name: Map
items.doc: An immutable, insertion-ordered map. Keys are `Eq + Hash`.

items.name: contains_key
items.receiver: impl[K: Eq + Hash, V] Map[K, V]
items.doc: True when `key` is present.

items.name: filter
items.receiver: impl[K: Eq + Hash, V] Map[K, V]
items.signature: fn filter(self, keep: fn(K, V) -> Bool) -> Map[K, V]
items.doc: The entries for which `keep` is true.

items.name: get
items.receiver: impl[K: Eq + Hash, V] Map[K, V]
items.doc: The value for `key`, or `None` when it is absent. `m[key]` panics instead.

items.name: insert
items.receiver: impl[K: Eq + Hash, V] Map[K, V]
items.signature: fn insert(self, key: K, value: V) -> Map[K, V]
items.doc: A copy with `key` set to `value` (a new key goes last; an existing key keeps its place).

items.name: is_empty
items.receiver: impl[K: Eq + Hash, V] Map[K, V]
items.doc: True when the map has no entries.

items.name: keys
items.receiver: impl[K: Eq + Hash, V] Map[K, V]
items.doc: The keys in insertion order.

items.name: len
items.receiver: impl[K: Eq + Hash, V] Map[K, V]
items.doc: The number of entries.

items.name: map
items.receiver: impl[K: Eq + Hash, V] Map[K, V]
items.signature: fn map[U](self, f: fn(V) -> U) -> Map[K, U]
items.doc: `f` applied to every value; keys and order are kept.

items.name: remove
items.receiver: impl[K: Eq + Hash, V] Map[K, V]
items.signature: fn remove(self, key: K) -> Map[K, V]
items.doc: A copy without `key`.

items.name: values
items.receiver: impl[K: Eq + Hash, V] Map[K, V]
items.doc: The values in insertion order.

items.name: Message
items.doc: Live-component messages (spec §20.3). Explicit `@derive(Message)`, enums only.

items.name: Net
items.doc: Outbound HTTP and listening sockets. TLS verification is always on.

items.name: allow_private
items.doc: A `Net` that may reach private address ranges (blocked by default, 04 S12).

items.name: only
items.doc: A `Net` that may reach only `hosts`.

items.name: Never
items.doc: The type with no values: the type of `panic(…)`, `return`, `break` and `continue`.

items.name: None
items.doc: The absent case of `Option`.

items.name: Ok
items.doc: The success case of `Result`.

items.name: Option
items.doc: `Some(value)` or `None`: the only absence value. The variants are the core constructors `Some` and `None` (spec §7.2), so they are not declared here.

items.name: expect
items.doc: The value. Panics with `reason` for `None`.

items.name: is_none
items.doc: True for `None`.

items.name: is_some
items.doc: True for `Some`.

items.name: map
items.signature: fn map[U](self, f: fn(T) -> U) -> Option[U]
items.doc: `Some(f(x))` for `Some(x)`, `None` for `None`.

items.name: ok_or
items.signature: fn ok_or[E](self, error: E) -> Result[T, E]
items.doc: `Ok(x)` for `Some(x)`, `Err(error)` for `None`.

items.name: or
items.doc: The value, or `default` for `None`.

items.name: Ord
items.doc: `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` and `sorted()`. Explicit `@derive(Ord)`: declaration order.

items.name: Ordering
items.doc: The result of a three-way comparison (`Float.total_cmp`, `List.sort_by` comparators).

items.name: Path
items.doc: A file path built by `path"…"`; holes must be `PathSegment`s. See std/path.

items.name: join
items.signature: fn join(base: Path, rel: Path) -> Result[Path, PathError]
items.doc: `rel` inside `base`. Refuses a result that escapes `base` (04 S13).

items.name: to_text
items.doc: The path as text, with `/` separators.

items.name: PathSegment
items.doc: One validated path component (no `/`, `\`, `.`, `..`, NUL or reserved name).

items.name: parse
items.doc: A single path component. Rejects the empty string, `.`, `..`, `/`, `\`, NUL, drive letters and Windows reserved names.

items.name: Proc
items.doc: Running `Command`s (never a shell).

items.name: only
items.doc: A `Proc` that may run only `programs`.

items.name: pipe
items.signature: fn pipe(self, commands: List[Command]) -> Result[Output, ProcError]
items.doc: Runs `commands` as a pipeline, each one's stdout feeding the next one's stdin.

items.name: run
items.signature: fn run(self, command: Command, env: Map[String, String] = {}) -> Result[Output, ProcError]
items.doc: Runs `command` to completion. The child gets an empty environment unless `env` is given. A whole-word hole value starting with `-` and not after a literal `--` is `Err(.OptionLikeArgument(index))`, and the process is not started.

items.name: Rand
items.doc: A cryptographically secure random number generator.

items.name: int
items.doc: A uniformly random integer in `range` (CSPRNG).

items.name: seeded
items.doc: A deterministic generator started from `seed`. Needs no capability.

items.name: token
items.doc: `bytes` random bytes as URL-safe base64 text.

items.name: uuid_v4
items.doc: A random version 4 UUID.

items.name: Range
items.doc: `a..b` (end excluded) and `a..=b` (end included).

items.name: Regex
items.doc: A linear-time (RE2) pattern built by `regex"…"` or `Regex.parse`.

items.name: matches
items.doc: True when the pattern matches somewhere in `text`.

items.name: parse
items.doc: Compiles a runtime pattern with the same engine as `regex"…"`.

items.name: replace
items.signature: fn replace(self, text: String, replacement: String) -> String
items.doc: `text` with every match replaced by `replacement` (taken literally).

items.name: RegexError
items.doc: Why `Regex.parse` rejected its pattern.

items.name: form
items.doc: The form body decoded into `T` (schema-first); a bad body is a 400.

items.name: header
items.doc: The request header `name`, or `None`.

items.name: json
items.doc: The JSON body decoded into `T` (schema-first, default limits); a bad body is a 400.

items.name: path
items.signature: fn path(self, name: String) -> Result[String, HttpError]
items.doc: The path parameter `name`.

items.name: path_int
items.signature: fn path_int(self, name: String) -> Result[Int, HttpError]
items.doc: The path parameter `name` as an `Int`; a bad value is a 400.

items.name: query
items.doc: The query string decoded into `T` (schema-first); a bad value is a 400.

items.name: query_param
items.doc: The first query parameter `name`, or `None`.

items.name: html
items.doc: A 200 response with an HTML page.

items.name: json
items.doc: A 200 response with `value` as JSON.

items.name: redirect
items.doc: A 303 redirect. `to` must be relative or on the app's allow-list (04 S17).

items.name: status
items.doc: The same response with another status code.

items.name: text
items.doc: A 200 response with plain text.

items.name: Result
items.doc: `Ok(value)` or `Err(error)`. Must-use (K1303). The variants are the core constructors `Ok` and `Err` (spec §7.2).

items.name: context
items.signature: fn context(self, message: String) -> Result[T, AnyError]
items.doc: The error boxed into `AnyError` with `message` added to its chain.

items.name: expect
items.doc: The value. Panics with `reason` for an `Err`.

items.name: is_err
items.doc: True for `Err`.

items.name: is_ok
items.doc: True for `Ok`.

items.name: map
items.signature: fn map[U](self, f: fn(T) -> U) -> Result[U, E]
items.doc: `Ok(f(x))` for `Ok(x)`; an `Err` is kept.

items.name: map_err
items.signature: fn map_err[F](self, f: fn(E) -> F) -> Result[T, F]
items.doc: `Err(f(e))` for `Err(e)`; an `Ok` is kept.

items.name: ok
items.doc: `Some(x)` for `Ok(x)`, `None` for an `Err`.

items.name: delete
items.signature: fn delete(self, path: String, handler: fn(Request[A]) -> Result[Response, HttpError], access: Access) -> Router[A]
items.doc: Adds a `DELETE` route.

items.name: get
items.signature: fn get(self, path: String, handler: fn(Request[A]) -> Result[Response, HttpError], access: Access) -> Router[A]
items.doc: Adds a `GET` route. Escape the braces of path parameters: `"/notes/\{id\}"`.

items.name: post
items.signature: fn post(self, path: String, handler: fn(Request[A]) -> Result[Response, HttpError], access: Access) -> Router[A]
items.doc: Adds a `POST` route.

items.name: put
items.signature: fn put(self, path: String, handler: fn(Request[A]) -> Result[Response, HttpError], access: Access) -> Router[A]
items.doc: Adds a `PUT` route.

items.name: Row
items.doc: Decoding SQL rows by column name. Explicit `@derive(Row)`.

items.name: Screen
items.doc: A canvas and input (`js-browser` only).

items.name: Secret
items.doc: A value that shows as `[REDACTED]`, has no `Encode`, and no `Eq`, `Ord` or `Hash`.

items.name: expose
items.doc: The wrapped value. An escape hatch counted by `kalam audit`.

items.name: new
items.doc: Wraps `value`.

items.name: float
items.doc: The next `Float` in [0, 1).

items.name: int
items.doc: The next integer in `range`.

items.name: Set
items.doc: An immutable, insertion-ordered set. Built with `Set.of([…])`.

items.name: contains
items.doc: True when `item` is in the set.

items.name: insert
items.doc: A copy with `item` added (no change when it is present).

items.name: intersection
items.doc: The elements of `self` that are also in `other`.

items.name: is_empty
items.doc: True when the set has no elements.

items.name: len
items.doc: The number of elements.

items.name: of
items.doc: A set of the distinct items, in order of first appearance.

items.name: remove
items.doc: A copy without `item`.

items.name: to_list
items.doc: The elements in insertion order.

items.name: union
items.doc: The elements of both sets: `self`'s first, then the new ones of `other`.

items.name: Show
items.doc: Text form used by interpolation, `print` and logs. Derived automatically.

items.name: Some
items.doc: The present case of `Option`.

items.name: Sql
items.doc: One SQL statement built by `sql"…"`; holes are bound parameters.

items.name: join
items.signature: fn join(parts: List[Sql], sep: Sql) -> Sql
items.doc: The fragments joined by `sep`.

items.name: SqlParam
items.doc: Types accepted in a `sql"…"` hole (spec §17.3).

items.name: StaticParts
items.doc: The literal text of a tagged literal. Only the compiler can create one (spec §17.2).

items.name: Stdin
items.doc: Reading standard input.

items.name: read_line
items.doc: The next line without its terminator, or `None` at the end of input.

items.name: String
items.doc: An immutable sequence of Unicode scalar values. Strings cannot be indexed (K0650).

items.name: arabic_fold
items.doc: Arabic letter forms unified (spec §5.3): hamza and alef forms, ى and ي, ة and ه.

items.name: byte_len
items.doc: The length of the UTF-8 encoding in bytes.

items.name: chars
items.doc: Each Unicode scalar value as a one-character string.

items.name: contains
items.doc: True when `part` occurs in the string.

items.name: ends_with
items.doc: True when the string ends with `suffix`.

items.name: graphemes
items.doc: Each user-perceived character (extended grapheme cluster).

items.name: is_empty
items.doc: True for the empty string.

items.name: join
items.signature: fn join(parts: List[String], sep: String) -> String
items.doc: The parts with `sep` between each two.

items.name: len_chars
items.doc: The number of Unicode scalar values.

items.name: nfc
items.doc: The NFC normal form. Equality is code-point equality, so normalize explicitly.

items.name: replace
items.signature: fn replace(self, old: String, new: String) -> String
items.doc: Every occurrence of `old` replaced by `new`.

items.name: slice
items.signature: fn slice(self, from: Int, to: Int) -> String
items.doc: The graphemes from index `from` up to, not including, `to`.

items.name: split
items.doc: The pieces between occurrences of `sep`.

items.name: starts_with
items.doc: True when the string begins with `prefix`.

items.name: to_decimal
items.doc: The exact `Decimal` written in the text.

items.name: to_float
items.doc: The `Float` written in the text.

items.name: to_int
items.doc: The integer written in the text: an optional `-`, then ASCII or Arabic-Indic digits. Text outside the `Int` range is an error, never a rounded value.

items.name: to_lower
items.doc: Lowercase (Unicode default case mapping).

items.name: to_upper
items.doc: Uppercase (Unicode default case mapping).

items.name: trim
items.doc: Without leading and trailing whitespace.

items.name: Template
items.doc: A user-defined tagged literal, registered with `@tag("name")` (spec §17.8).

items.name: build
items.signature: fn build(parts: StaticParts, holes: List[TemplateHole]) -> Self

items.name: TemplateHole
items.doc: One typed hole of a tagged literal, passed to `Template.build`.

items.name: Url
items.doc: A URL built by `url"…"` or `Url.parse`. It never holds `javascript:`, `data:` or `vbscript:` unless built with `unsafe.raw_url`.

items.name: parse
items.doc: Parses and validates a runtime URL.

items.name: UrlError
items.doc: Why `Url.parse` rejected its input.

items.name: World
items.doc: The root capability. Only `main` receives it; it cannot be constructed or decoded (K1501).

items.name: screen
items.signature: fn screen(self, width: Int, height: Int) -> Screen
items.doc: A canvas and input capability (`js-browser` target only, K1502 elsewhere).

items.name: named
items.doc: The IANA zone with this name, such as `Africa/Cairo`.

items.name: utc
items.doc: Coordinated Universal Time.

items.name: assert
items.doc: Panics with `message` when `condition` is false.

items.name: panic
items.doc: Stops the current task with a defined panic. It cannot be caught.

items.name: print
items.doc: Writes the value's `Show` text and a newline to standard output.

items.name: bigint
items.doc: std/bigint (spec §9.2, §20.1): methods of the prelude type `BigInt`. The arithmetic operators work as for `Int`, without overflow.

items.name: decimal
items.doc: std/decimal (spec §9.2, §20.1): methods of the prelude type `Decimal`. `+ - *` are exact and trap on overflow; there is no `/` (04 L14).

items.name: Rounding
items.doc: How `div` and `round` choose between the two nearest results.

items.name: env
items.doc: std/env (spec §16.1, §18.1, §20.1): methods of the prelude capability `Env`.

items.name: fs
items.doc: std/fs (spec §16.1, §17.6, §20.1): methods of the prelude capability `Fs`. Paths are `Path` values (`path"…"`, `Path.join`), never `String`s.

items.name: FsError
items.doc: Why a file operation failed.

items.name: http
items.doc: std/http (spec §14.3, §16.3, §20.1, §20.2): routes, requests, responses, the server and an SSRF-blocking client. Routes are deny-by-default: `access:` has no default.

items.name: Access
items.doc: Who may call a route. `.LoggedIn` and `.Role` use the session middleware of std/auth.

items.name: ClientError
items.doc: Why an outbound request failed. Private address ranges are blocked unless the `Net` was attenuated with `allow_private` (04 S12).

items.name: ClientResponse
items.doc: What an outbound request returned.

items.name: HttpError
items.doc: The error side of a handler. Each variant maps to one HTTP status.

items.name: Request
items.doc: One incoming request. `app` is the record given to `serve`; it reaches the capabilities. Only the server creates requests.

items.name: Response
items.doc: An outgoing response.

items.name: Router
items.doc: A set of routes for an app record `A`.

items.name: ServeError
items.doc: Why the server could not start or stopped.

items.name: get
items.signature: fn get(net: Net, url: Url) -> Result[ClientResponse, ClientError]
items.doc: Sends a `GET` request.

items.name: post
items.signature: fn post(net: Net, url: Url, body: String) -> Result[ClientResponse, ClientError]
items.doc: Sends a `POST` request with a text body.

items.name: router
items.doc: A new router with the session middleware of std/auth installed.

items.name: serve
items.signature: fn serve[A](net: Net, port: Int, router: Router[A], app: A) -> Result[(), ServeError]
items.doc: Serves `router` on `port` until the process stops.

items.name: json
items.doc: std/json (spec §18.3, §20.1). Part of the prelude as the module `json`. Decoding is schema-first: it builds exactly the expected type `T` and nothing the payload names.

items.name: DecodeError
items.doc: Why a decode failed. Unknown fields, duplicate keys, fractions or exponents for an `Int`, integers outside the `Int` range, NaN and Infinity are all rejected.

items.name: DecodeLimits
items.doc: Limits for one decode. The defaults are the spec's (1 MiB, depth 32, 10,000 elements per container, 64 KiB per string).

items.name: decode
items.signature: fn decode[T: Decode](input: String, limits: DecodeLimits = DecodeLimits()) -> Result[T, DecodeError]
items.doc: The `T` (taken from the expected type) that `input` describes.

items.name: encode
items.doc: JSON text for `value`.

items.name: list
items.doc: std/list (spec §9.3, §10.8, §20.1): methods of the prelude type `List[T]`. Lists are immutable: every "change" returns a new list (`items = items.append(x)`).

items.name: log
items.doc: std/log (spec §16.4, §20.1). Part of the prelude as the module `log`. Ambient console output (D20): structured lines on stderr, `Secret` values redacted, CR/LF and ANSI sequences escaped. A library that calls these must declare `console = true`.

items.name: debug
items.signature: fn debug(message: String, fields: Map[String, String] = {})
items.doc: A debugging detail.

items.name: error
items.signature: fn error(message: String, fields: Map[String, String] = {})
items.doc: A failure.

items.name: info
items.signature: fn info(message: String, fields: Map[String, String] = {})
items.doc: A normal event.

items.name: warn
items.signature: fn warn(message: String, fields: Map[String, String] = {})
items.doc: Something unexpected that the program handled.

items.name: map
items.doc: std/map (spec §9.3, §10.4, §10.8, §20.1): methods of the prelude type `Map[K, V]`. Maps are immutable and insertion-ordered; `m[k] = v` on a `var` means `m = m.insert(k, v)`. Iterating yields `(key, value)` pairs in insertion order.

items.name: math
items.doc: std/math (spec §20.1). There is no overloading, so each function has one type.

items.name: PI
items.doc: The ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter.

items.name: abs
items.doc: The absolute value of an `Int`. Panics on the minimum `Int`.

items.name: clamp
items.signature: fn clamp[T: Ord](x: T, low: T, high: T) -> T
items.doc: `x` limited to the range `low..=high`.

items.name: floor
items.doc: The largest integral value not greater than `x`.

items.name: max
items.signature: fn max[T: Ord](a: T, b: T) -> T
items.doc: The larger of `a` and `b` (`a` when they are equal).

items.name: min
items.signature: fn min[T: Ord](a: T, b: T) -> T
items.doc: The smaller of `a` and `b` (`a` when they are equal).

items.name: pow
items.signature: fn pow(base: Float, exponent: Float) -> Float
items.doc: `base` raised to the power `exponent`.

items.name: round
items.doc: The nearest integral value; halves round away from zero.

items.name: sqrt
items.doc: The square root (NaN for negative input).

items.name: option
items.doc: std/option (spec §9.3, §11 rule 12, §14.4, §20.1): methods of the prelude type `Option[T]`. There is no bare `unwrap()`: `expect` requires a reason (K0915).

items.name: path
items.doc: std/path (spec §17.6, §20.1): methods of the prelude types `Path` and `PathSegment`.

items.name: PathError
items.doc: Why a path or path segment was rejected.

items.name: prelude
items.doc: The prelude (spec §13.1, §7.2, §9, §16, §17). Every module imports it implicitly. M2 signature stubs: `@builtin` items are provided by the compiler and the runtime, and the `panic("builtin")` bodies are placeholders. See stdlib/README.md for the conventions.

items.name: proc
items.doc: std/proc (spec §17.5, §20.1): methods of the prelude capability `Proc`. Kalam never runs a shell: a `Command` is a program plus argv, built by `cmd"…"`.

items.name: Output
items.doc: What a finished process produced.

items.name: ProcError
items.doc: Why a process did not run or did not finish.

items.name: random
items.doc: std/random (spec §16.1, §18.2): methods of the prelude capability `Rand`, plus the deterministic `SeededRand`. `SeededRand` needs no capability and has no `token` or `uuid_v4`, so using it for secrets is a type error by omission (04 S7).

items.name: SeededRand
items.doc: A deterministic pseudo-random generator for games, simulations and tests. Each draw advances its internal state; the same seed gives the same sequence.

items.name: result
items.doc: std/result (spec §9.3, §14, §20.1): methods of the prelude type `Result[T, E]`. A `Result` is must-use (K1303); `let _ = r` discards one deliberately.

items.name: set
items.doc: std/set (spec §9.3, §20.1): methods of the prelude type `Set[T]`. Sets are immutable and insertion-ordered.

items.name: sql
items.doc: std/sql (spec §16.1, §17.3, §20.1): databases. Every query is a `Sql` value from `sql"…"` (holes are bound parameters) or `sql.ident`; a `String` is never a query (K1601). The module `sql` and the tag `sql` live in different namespaces (spec §17.1).

items.name: Db
items.doc: A database connection or open transaction. Built from a capability by `sqlite` or `postgres`; a library that needs a database takes a `Db`.

items.name: DbError
items.doc: Why a database call failed.

items.name: LikePattern
items.doc: A `LIKE` pattern with `%`, `_` and `\` escaped, made by `like_contains`, `like_prefix` or `like_suffix`. It is a bound parameter; a raw `String` in a `LIKE` hole is W1606.

items.name: ident
items.signature: fn ident(name: String, allowed: List[String]) -> Result[Sql, DbError]
items.doc: `name` as an SQL identifier, only when it is one of `allowed`.

items.name: like_contains
items.doc: A `LIKE` pattern matching text that contains `text` (`%`, `_` and `\` escaped).

items.name: like_prefix
items.doc: A `LIKE` pattern matching text that starts with `text`.

items.name: like_suffix
items.doc: A `LIKE` pattern matching text that ends with `text`.

items.name: postgres
items.signature: fn postgres(net: Net, url: Secret[String]) -> Result[Db, DbError]
items.doc: Connects to Postgres. TLS verification is always on.

items.name: sqlite
items.signature: fn sqlite(fs: Fs, file: String) -> Result[Db, DbError]
items.doc: Opens (or creates) the SQLite database file `file` under `fs`.

items.name: string
items.doc: std/string (spec §9.2, §20.1): methods of the prelude type `String`. Method resolution never depends on imports (DR-27), so these work without `use std/string`.

items.name: ParseError
items.doc: Why `to_int`, `to_float` or `to_decimal` rejected its text.

items.name: task
items.doc: std/task (spec §15.7, §20.1): structured concurrency, plus `Cell`. At M2 it re-exports the prelude's `Cell` (FOUNDER-QUEUE Q46), so `use std/task.{Cell}` works; the §15.7 functions (`task.all`, `task.both`, `task.race`, `task.timeout`, `task.sleep`, `task.scope`) are added with the runtime that runs them.

items.name: time
items.doc: std/time (spec §16.1, §20.1). Reading the time needs the `Clock` capability; `Duration` arithmetic, dates and formatting are ambient.

items.name: Date
items.doc: A calendar date (proleptic Gregorian) with no time of day.

items.name: Duration
items.doc: A length of time, possibly negative.

items.name: Instant
items.doc: A point in time (UTC, nanosecond precision).

items.name: TimeError
items.doc: Why a time zone or date could not be read.

items.name: Zone
items.doc: A time zone from the IANA database.
